title: Don Isaac Abravanel
hook: a royal minister who chose exile with his people

segments.voice: Yesterday, 1492: the order that ended open Jewish life in Spain. Your line was the key on the nail. Today, one man who could have stayed behind, and didn't.

A man stands in a royal palace with a purse he hopes will change a king's mind. He has served the crown of Castile with money and with figures; the rulers know him by name. The order to expel the Jews has been signed, and he has come to plead. Tradition says he offered a great sum, and that for a moment it seemed to work. Then the door closed. Some tellings say he could have kept his place at court, if he would be baptized.
screen: `A PURSE AND A PLEA.` → `THE DOOR CLOSES.` → `A PLACE AT COURT, FOR A PRICE.`

segments.voice: Don is a Spanish title of honor. Isaac Abravanel was a financier who had served rulers in Portugal and then in Spain, and also a scholar who wrote long commentaries on the books of the Bible. In the preface to his commentary on the book of Kings, he tells the story in his own words: how he went before the king again and again, how he begged, how friends at court pleaded too, and how none of it moved the decree. Another court Jew he had worked beside, Abraham Seneor, accepted baptism and stayed. Abravanel did not. He left Spain with the rest of the exiles, carrying his books, and spent his last years moving from city to city, Naples, Corfu, Monopoli and at last Venice, still writing. His commentaries are still read and printed today, and they open with long lists of questions before he answers any of them. The book of Ruth has a line that fits. Ruth, a widow from Moab, is told she may go back to her own home. She answers her mother-in-law: "whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God." Ruth chose a people she was not born into. Abravanel chose the people he was born into, at the moment it cost him everything the court could give. He did not save the community; he failed at that. What he did was refuse to be saved apart from them.
screen: `A MINISTER AND A SCHOLAR.` · `HE PLEADED WITH THE KING.` · `A COLLEAGUE STAYED. HE DID NOT.` · then, large: `WHITHER THOU GOEST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the people you belong to, a family, a congregation, a neighborhood, a crew at work, and picture them walking a road together. See yourself in that line, not watching from a window, and if you pray, say Ruth's words quietly: thy people shall be my people.
Abravanel. A minister of kings and a Bible commentator who pleaded against the 1492 expulsion, failed, and chose exile with the people he could not save. Today's word.
Your line: he left with them. He couldn't save them, so he went where they went. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Abravanel's Bible commentaries are still studied, and his own account of the expulsion is read by those who study the Spanish exile; some Jews remember the expulsion on Tisha B'Av.
